headline: Nominated Craig Tufts and Ian McGregor to Planning Board's Master Plan Advisory Subcommittee; discussed sidewalks and Loudon Road.
summary: Members discussed the Green Street sidewalks, Loudon Road, and existing master plan projects. They approved the July 23, 2026 minutes and nominated Craig Tufts, with Ian McGregor as alternate, to the Planning Board's Master Plan Advisory Subcommittee.
decisions: Nominated Craig Tufts as representative and Ian McGregor as alternate to the Planning Board's Master Plan Advisory Subcommittee; motion passed unanimously.

plain_text:
September 24, 2026 
Page 1 of 4 
 
CITY OF CONCORD 
TRANSPORTATION POLICY ADVISORY COMMITTEE 
MINUTES OF SEPTEMBER 24, 2026 
 
The Transportation Policy Advisory Committee (TPAC) met at 6:00 pm on September 24, 2026 
in City Council Chambers, 37 Green Street 
 
Members 
Present: 
Greg Bakos (Chair), Marcus Flynn, Nicole Fox, Ian McGregor, Chris Nadeau, Erika 
Rydberg-Hall, Councilor Schultz, Ganesh Sharma, Mickey Shoemaker, Craig Tufts 
  
Members 
Absent: 
 
Councilor Foote, Councilor Todd (Vice-Chair) 
Guests: Eric Gallagher (Outgoing Ward 6 State Representative, interested in Public Transit 
Subcommittee) 
 
City Staff: Mike Bezanson (City Engineer), Karen Hill (Transportation Engineer), Alec Bass 
(Assistant City Planner – Community Planning) 
 
1.   Call to Order 
   Chair Bakos called the meeting to order at 6:03 pm.  
 
2.    Introductions 
 
3.   Approval of Minutes 
   Approval of Minutes – July 23, 2026 
On a motion made by Schultz, seconded by Flynn, the meeting minutes of July 23, 2026 
were approved. 
 
4.   Public Comment 
   Eric Gallagher, speaking as a resident, asked what was going on with the sidewalk 
improvements on Green Street.  
 
Bakos explained the project and its history at the Committee and Council. He expressed 
that it will be great when it is complete, as it is intended to calm traffic and improve 
pedestrian safety. 
 
Gallagher mentioned that a map of proposed sidewalks was presented at the 
September 19, 2026 Master Planning Session and asked for it to be displayed on the 
screen. He pointed out the top ten sidewalk segments. He mentioned that he recently 
proposed a bill that would allow municipalities to build sidewalks on State property, 
which would allow the segment along Pleasant Street to be built, but it did not pass due 
to a technicality. He feels this is an important segment. 
 
Gallagher supports the proposed sidewalk segment along Clinton Street. He also feels 
that closing the gaps along South and South Main Streets is important because 
pedestrians currently need to cross back and forth to utilize the sidewalk.
September 24, 2026 
Page 2 of 4 
 
 
He believes the Airport Road sidewalk should be extended to complete the connection 
to Manchester Street and asked if Manchester Street will receive sidewalk. 
 
Hill replied that the City does have a CIP project, which will include State funding, to 
provide sidewalk on both sides of Manchester Street. She also added that the sidewalk 
on Airport Road currently ends at its present location because that was the limit of the 
road resurfacing project at the time. 
 
Schultz noted that Gallagher takes many walks and provides social media coverage of 
the sidewalk networks throughout Concord.  
 
Sharma observed that many of the priorities appear to be in the south end of Concord 
and asked why. 
 
Hill shared that the master plan board presented only 8 sidewalk examples; the 
complete list is available in the 2017 Pedestrian Master Plan.  
 
5.   TPAC Referrals from City Council, Staff and Chair 
   None. 
 
6.   Unfinished Business (continued from July 23, 2026) 
 a.  Loudon Road Corridor discussion  
Hill shared that she is working with a consultant to get a scope for the traffic signal 
warrant analysis at Woodcrest Heights Road and Loudon Road.  
 
Fox mentioned that Concord Greenspace conducted a walk audit of Loudon Road from 
the Merrimack River to D’Amante Drive, in which 25 members of the public 
participated. She said they plan to summarize and present the results in a report. She 
noted that a temporary sidewalk condition led to some complications for one 
participant who travels in a motorized wheelchair. Fox acknowledged the challenge but 
confirmed that it was resolved by the City the following day. 
 
Bakos noted that improvements to the Loudon Road corridor should not be lost and 
suggested that they remain a priority in the upcoming master plan. 
 
Schultz referred back to the individual who presented concerns about the Gully Hill area 
and inquired about potential short-term, low-cost improvements. 
 
Bakos stated that Staff has already narrowed lanes in the area and that, because the 
area has minimal interruptions and friction, it would be difficult to address driver 
behavior with low-cost solutions. He also mentioned the prior concept to construct a 
multi-use path in this area and felt that it should be discussed during the upcoming 
master plan process. 
 
Hill noted that the Loudon Road lane reduction was in the previous master plan.
September 24, 2026 
Page 3 of 4 
 
 b.  Review current Master Plan projects and status 
The Committee entered a working session to review the short- and long-term projects 
in the existing master plan. Members shared their thoughts and comments on each 
project, and Hill recorded a list of projects and comments for continued discussion at 
the next meeting and eventual sharing with Council. 
 
The Committee had several questions about the Garvins Falls Urban Reserve Area Study 
and associated projects. Bass will share a link to the study for Members to review prior 
to the next meeting. 
 
The work session ended at the long-term I-93 improvement items, and the Committee 
will continue its evaluation next month.  
 
7.   New Business 
 a.  Request from Planning Board to nominate member(s) to serve on the Planning Board’s 
Master Plan Advisory Subcommittee 
Bakos made a motion, seconded by Flynn, to nominate Craig Tufts as the TPAC 
representative and Ian McGregor to serve as the alternate. All in favor. The motion 
passed unanimously. 
    
8.   Consent Reports 
   None. 
    
9.   General Updates 
 a.  City Council Meeting 
Schultz shared that the report from TPAC regarding the Middle School Project was 
discussed and that Council appreciated the work, listening, and effort undertaken by 
TPAC. Hill explained that the report was accepted by Council and noted that the City 
Manager has sent a letter to the School District requesting a response. 
 
Schultz, Tufts, and McGregor briefly discussed the proposed bike park at Russell Martin 
Park, which was discussed at Council.  
 
 b.  Bicycle/Pedestrian Subcommittee (TPAC-BP) 
No meeting. 
 
 c.  Traffic Operations Committee (TOC) 
Hill shared that meeting minutes are available on the City’s website. 
 
 d.  Public Transportation (CAT) 
Schultz noted that she is meeting with Terri Paige, CAT, next week to plan for the 
subcommittee’s first meeting.  
 
10.   Project Updates (Staff)   
    Hill noted that the Green Street and associated sidewalk improvements are underway. 
She also noted that the Broadway/Wiggin improvements are under construction and 
will be completed shortly.
September 24, 2026 
Page 4 of 4 
 
 
Bezanson stated that the Loudon Road Bridge project is awaiting a grant decision and 
that he hopes to hear back within 3 weeks. 
 
Hill shared an update on the ornamental streetlight replacement project along Loudon 
Road and Manchester Street. She mentioned a material delay, but the City is hoping to 
install the lights in November.  
 
11.   Other Discussion Items 
None. 
 
12.   Adjourn 
   On a motion made by Bakos, seconded by Schultz, the meeting adjourned at 7:39 pm by 
unanimous consent. 
 
13.   Next Meeting   
October 22, 2026 
 
Minutes prepared by Alec Bass and Karen Hill.
